newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Death toll in Russia blast at 68, rescue work ends.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Russia blast at 68, rescue work ends.

text.p: The death toll from a weekend explosion in Russia's southern Dagestan region rose to 68 on Tuesday and rescue workers gave up hope of finding more survivors from the blast, believed to be an act of sabotage.

A spokesman for the regional authorities told Reuters by telephone that the rescue teams had halted their round-the-clock search for survivors amid the rubble of the military apartment block in the town of Kaspiysk.
Parts of the building still standing after the blast had been torn down and investigators now planned to search the basement for traces of an explosive device, he said.
Eight people, including four children, were being treated in hospital. Around 20 children were among the dead, he added.
The blast occurred early on Saturday when residents, mainly border guards and their families, were sleeping. The concrete- panelled nine-storey building collapsed like a pack of cards.

Itar-Tass news agency said 54 of those killed were military personnel and some officials have suggested the blast was a gangland revenge attack following a regional crackdown by the border guards on arms and caviar smuggling.
Others believe that explosives could have been stored in the building. The block was built in such a way that it would have been unable to withstand even a minor blast.

Rebel leaders in breakaway Chechnya, which borders Dagestan, have angrily denied suggestions that they were responsible for the blast. They counter that it could have been aimed at derailing peace talks.
However, they said, they could not rule out that go-it-alone separatist fighters arranged the explosion.

RIA news agency quoted the Dagestani interior minister Mahomed Abdurazakov as saying three people had been detained on suspicion of involvement in the blast. The authorities have already released one man wrongly believed to be implicated.

President Boris Yeltsin declared Tuesday a day of national mourning. He ordered flags to fly at half-mast across the Russian Federation and asked mass media to cancel light entertainment programmes as a mark of respect.
